ललल्लम्बस्तनीं दृष्ट्वा जरा योषापि नृत्यति ॥ 14 ॥
4.134.m:
In this way, people in these three worlds are fully engaged in this.
Seeing her dangling, drooping breasts, even an old woman dances!

4.134.s:
vasaṃtasya prabhāvo'yaṃ ko'pyapūrvo vijṛṃbhate ..
sarāṃsyadbhutapadmāni praphullā puṣpavāṭikāḥ .. 15 ..
4.134.d:
वसंतस्य प्रभावोऽयं कोऽप्यपूर्वो विजृंभते ॥
सरांस्यद्भुतपद्मानि प्रफुल्ला पुष्पवाटिकाः ॥ 15 ॥
4.134.m:
Such an extraordinary, unprecedented power of Spring manifests itself:
lakes with wondrous lotuses, flower gardens in full bloom,

4.134.s:
vṛkṣāḥ pakṣiśatākīrṇā vijighrāṇamukhāḥ surāḥ ..
vikaṃpavasanāvālaḥ pavanastriguṇātmakaḥ ..16..
4.134.d:
वृक्षाः पक्षिशताकीर्णा विजिघ्राणमुखाः सुराः ॥
विकंपवसनावालः पवनस्त्रिगुणात्मकः ॥16॥
4.134.m:
trees thronged with hundreds of birds, gods with smelling faces,
and the three-natured wind stirring the garments and hair.

4.134.s:
kṛtaḥ pratyakṣasumahānvasaṃto na jagattraye ..
avajalpamukhā bālā vṛddhāstu vikaladvijāḥ .. 17 ..
4.134.d:
कृतः प्रत्यक्षसुमहान्वसंतो न जगत्त्रये ॥
अवजल्पमुखा बाला वृद्धास्तु विकलद्विजाः ॥ 17 ॥
4.134.m:
Has not an exceedingly great Spring been made visible in the three worlds?
Children with babbling mouths, and the aged with failing teeth,

4.134.s:
ubhāvapi pratapyete paśyedaṃ kāmaceṣṭitam ..
pakṣiṇāṃ pakṣanikṣepairnadyastuṃgataraṃgakaiḥ .. 18 ..
4.134.d:
उभावपि प्रतप्येते पश्येदं कामचेष्टितम् ॥
पक्षिणां पक्षनिक्षेपैर्नद्यस्तुंगतरंगकैः ॥ 18 ॥
4.134.m:
both are tormented—behold this doing of Kāma!
With the flapping of the wings of birds, with the rivers' soaring waves,

4.134.s:
pādapāḥ pallavaśatairnṛtyaṃte ca praharṣiṇaḥ ..
etacchrutvā tu vacanaṃ nāradasyenduśekharaḥ .. 19 ..
4.134.d:
पादपाः पल्लवशतैर्नृत्यंते च प्रहर्षिणः ॥
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं नारदस्येन्दुशेखरः ॥ 19 ॥
4.134.m:
and the trees with hundreds of sprouts, they dance in great joy.
Having heard these words of Nārada, the Moon-crested Lord,

4.134.s:
kautukākulitaḥ śīghramāruroha rathaṃ svakam ..
rathena kāñcanāṃgena patatrivaraketanaḥ .. 4.134.20 ..
4.134.d:
कौतुकाकुलितः शीघ्रमारुरोह रथं स्वकम् ॥
रथेन काञ्चनांगेन पतत्रिवरकेतनः ॥ 4.134.20 ॥
4.134.m:
filled with curiosity, swiftly mounted his own chariot.
Upon a chariot with golden limbs, he whose emblem is the best of birds,

4.134.s:
prayayau puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ śaṃkhacakragadādharaḥ ..
pārāvatapratīkāśaṃ caturvedamayaṃ ratham .. 21 ..
4.134.d:
प्रययौ पुण्डरीकाक्षः शंखचक्रगदाधरः ॥
पारावतप्रतीकाशं चतुर्वेदमयं रथम् ॥ 21 ॥
4.134.m:
the lotus-eyed wielder of the conch, discus, and mace, set forth;
mounting a chariot resembling a dove and consisting of the four Vedas,

4.134.s:
āsthāya prayayau hṛṣṭo brahmā brāhmaṇasaṃstutaḥ ..
munibhiścāpsarobhiśca yakṣarakṣomahoragaiḥ .. 22 ..
4.134.d:
आस्थाय प्रययौ हृष्टो ब्रह्मा ब्राह्मणसंस्तुतः ॥
मुनिभिश्चाप्सरोभिश्च यक्षरक्षोमहोरगैः ॥ 22 ॥
4.134.m:
delighted Brahmā, praised by Brahmins, set forth,
surrounded by sages, apsarases, yakṣas, rakṣasas, and great serpents.

4.134.s:
vṛto rathena prayayau bhāskaro vāritaskaraḥ ..
śailajorupatākena rathenādityavarcasā .. 23 ..
4.134.d:
वृतो रथेन प्रययौ भास्करो वारितस्करः ॥
शैलजोरुपताकेन रथेनादित्यवर्चसा ॥ 23 ॥
4.134.m:
Mounted on a chariot, the Sun, who drives away thieves, set forth.
In a chariot with the splendour of the sun and with the large banner of the Mountain's Daughter,

4.134.s:
kātyāyanī pracalitā pañcavaktreṇa ketunā ..
laṃbodaraḥ karaśatagṛhītakanakotpalaḥ .. 24 ..
4.134.d:
कात्यायनी प्रचलिता पञ्चवक्त्रेण केतुना ॥
लंबोदरः करशतगृहीतकनकोत्पलः ॥ 24 ॥
4.134.m:
Kātyāyanī set out, with her five-faced emblem.
The pot-bellied god, holding golden lotuses in hundreds of hands,

4.134.s:
prayātaḥ svarathārūḍhaḥ kṛtakarṇakulākulaḥ ..
evaṃ devaḥ parivṛto bhagavāngovṛṣadhvajaḥ .. 25 ..
4.134.d:
प्रयातः स्वरथारूढः कृतकर्णकुलाकुलः ॥
एवं देवः परिवृतो भगवान्गोवृषध्वजः ॥ 25 ॥
4.134.m:
mounted upon his chariot, with ears flapping busily, departed.
Thus surrounded, the blessed god whose banner bears the bull,

4.134.s:
rathārūḍhairamūḍhātmā martyalokamavātarat ..
yāvatpaśyati deveśastāvatsarvaṃ tadakṣaram .. 26 ..
4.134.d:
रथारूढैरमूढात्मा मर्त्यलोकमवातरत् ॥
यावत्पश्यति देवेशस्तावत्सर्वं तदक्षरम् ॥ 26 ॥
4.134.m:
unbewildered in mind, descended to the mortal world accompanied by those mounted on chariots.
As soon as the lord of gods looked, everything was indeed indestructible;

4.134.s:
nāradena yathaivoktastāvatsarvaṃ tadakṣaram ..
nāradena yathaivoktaṃ jagadānandanirbharam .. 27 ..
4.134.d:
नारदेन यथैवोक्तस्तावत्सर्वं तदक्षरम् ॥
नारदेन यथैवोक्तं जगदानन्दनिर्भरम् ॥ 27 ॥
4.134.m:
just as was spoken by Nārada, so was everything without fail;
just as was spoken by Nārada, the world was filled with bliss.

4.134.s:
devaiḥ sārddhaṃ paśupatiryāvatpaśyati vismitaḥ ..
tāvattasyaiva hi gaṇāḥ parabrahmasamaṃjasam .. 28 ..
4.134.d:
देवैः सार्द्धं पशुपतिर्यावत्पश्यति विस्मितः ॥
तावत्तस्यैव हि गणाः परब्रह्मसमंजसम् ॥ 28 ॥
4.134.m:
While Paśupati, astonished, looked on together with the gods,
right then his very own gaṇas, properly attuned to the supreme Brahman,

4.134.s:
gāyaṃti kecitsotkaṃṭhaṃ luṭhaṃtyanye praharṣitāḥ ..
vādayaṃtyapare tuṣṭā jahasuḥ kecidulbaṇam .. 29 ..
4.134.d:
गायंति केचित्सोत्कंठं लुठंत्यन्ये प्रहर्षिताः ॥
वादयंत्यपरे तुष्टा जहसुः केचिदुल्बणम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.134.m:
some were singing with longing, others were rolling on the ground in joy,
others, contented, were playing instruments, and some laughed boisterously.

4.134.s:
vādayaṃtyanyathā vādyaṃ gāyaṃtyanyenyathā gaṇāḥ ..
anyenyathā pranṛtyaṃti citraṃ caitrasya ceṣṭitam .. 4.134.30 ..
4.134.d:
वादयंत्यन्यथा वाद्यं गायंत्यन्येन्यथा गणाः ॥
अन्येन्यथा प्रनृत्यंति चित्रं चैत्रस्य चेष्टितम् ॥ 4.134.30 ॥
4.134.m:
The gaṇas played instruments in unusual ways, others sang in strange fashions,
and others danced in varied styles—wondrous was the sport of Caitra!

4.134.s:
nīlotpalābhanayanairvilasatprāṃtatārakaiḥ ..
krīḍāratibhirārabdhamālāpaiśca surairapi .. 31 ..
4.134.d:
नीलोत्पलाभनयनैर्विलसत्प्रांततारकैः ॥
क्रीडारतिभिरारब्धमालापैश्च सुरैरपि ॥ 31 ॥
4.134.m:
With eyes like blue lotuses, their outer pupils sparkling,
even the gods began to converse, delighting in playful revelry.

4.134.s:
surāṇāṃ kṣobhamālakṣya bhagavāngovṛṣadhvajaḥ ..
cintayāmāsa sumahānkāryayogo hyupasthitaḥ .. 32 ..
4.134.d:
सुराणां क्षोभमालक्ष्य भगवान्गोवृषध्वजः ॥
चिन्तयामास सुमहान्कार्ययोगो ह्युपस्थितः ॥ 32 ॥
4.134.m:
Observing the agitation of the gods, the blessed Lord whose banner bears the bull
thought: “A great confluence of duties is indeed present.”

4.134.s:
anarthamutthitaṃ tadvattadvighātāya ye janāḥ ..
nayaṃte ye'timūrkhatvādāpado'bhibhavaṃti tān .. 33 ..
4.134.d:
अनर्थमुत्थितं तद्वत्तद्विघाताय ये जनाः ॥
नयंते येऽतिमूर्खत्वादापदोऽभिभवंति तान् ॥ 33 ॥
4.134.m:
“Those people who bring about calamity that has arisen, or who out of extreme foolishness
do nothing to avert it, calamities overcome them.

4.134.s:
vasaṃtaḥ svāmibhaktatvānmānyapuṣpākaraṃ yadā ..
unmādāḍhyajano rakṣyaḥ kāryaṃ kāryadvayaṃ mama .. 34 ..
4.134.d:
वसंतः स्वामिभक्तत्वान्मान्यपुष्पाकरं यदा ॥
उन्मादाढ्यजनो रक्ष्यः कार्यं कार्यद्वयं मम ॥ 34 ॥
4.134.m:
Since Spring is devoted to his master, the spring season is to be honoured;
and people filled with madness must be protected: I have two tasks to perform.”

4.134.s:
saṃciṃtyaivaṃ samānāyya vasaṃtaṃ prāha śaṃkaraḥ ..
samānīto māsamekaṃ sthātavyaṃ bhavatā tviha .. 35 ..
4.134.d:
संचिंत्यैवं समानाय्य वसंतं प्राह शंकरः ॥
समानीतो मासमेकं स्थातव्यं भवता त्विह ॥ 35 ॥
4.134.m:
Having thus reflected and summoned Spring, Śaṅkara said to him:
“You have been brought here; you must remain in this place for one month.

4.134.s:
sitapakṣaḥ sahāyo'yaṃ sarvabhūtasukhapradaḥ ..
bhavatyatimahānando viśeṣeṇa divaukasām .. 36 ..
4.134.d:
सितपक्षः सहायोऽयं सर्वभूतसुखप्रदः ॥
भवत्यतिमहानन्दो विशेषेण दिवौकसाम् ॥ 36 ॥
4.134.m:
This companion, the bright fortnight, gives happiness to all beings;
and an exceedingly great joy arises, especially for the heaven-dwellers.

4.134.s:
yo yathā rathamārūḍhaḥ samāyātaḥ samīkṣitum ..
varṣevarṣe sa tenaiva saṃsthānenāgamiṣyati .. 37 ..
4.134.d:
यो यथा रथमारूढः समायातः समीक्षितुम् ॥
वर्षेवर्षे स तेनैव संस्थानेनागमिष्यति ॥ 37 ॥
4.134.m:
Whosoever came mounted on a chariot to observe [this spectacle],
he shall arrive year after year in that very same manner.

4.134.s:
kārayiṣyanti ye martyā rathayātrāmahotsavam ..
te divyabhogabhoktāro bhaviṣyanti nirāmayāḥ .. 38 ..
4.134.d:
कारयिष्यन्ति ये मर्त्या रथयात्रामहोत्सवम् ॥
ते दिव्यभोगभोक्तारो भविष्यन्ति निरामयाः ॥ 38 ॥
4.134.m:
Those mortals who perform the great festival of the chariot procession
shall enjoy divine pleasures and be free from affliction.”

4.134.s:
evamābhāṣya bhagavānvasaṃtaṃ ca tataḥ suraiḥ ..
saṃstuto'tha nataścāpi svasthānamagamattataḥ .. 39 ..
4.134.d:
एवमाभाष्य भगवान्वसंतं च ततः सुरैः ॥
संस्तुतोऽथ नतश्चापि स्वस्थानमगमत्ततः ॥ 39 ॥
4.134.m:
Having spoken thus to Spring, the blessed Lord, praised and bowed to
by the gods, then went to his own abode.

4.134.s:
.. yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
rathaḥ kimātmakaḥ kāryaḥ kāryā yātrā kathaṃ bhavet ..
āropayetkathaṃ devānrathe vada jagatpate .. 4.134.40 ..
4.134.d:
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
रथः किमात्मकः कार्यः कार्या यात्रा कथं भवेत् ॥
आरोपयेत्कथं देवान्रथे वद जगत्पते ॥ 4.134.40 ॥
4.134.m:
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
Of what nature should the chariot be made? How should the procession be carried out?
How should one mount the gods upon the chariot? Speak, O Lord of the universe!

4.134.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
suvicitraṃ citratanuṃ śreṣṭhakāṣṭhamayaṃ ratham ..
sudṛḍhākṣaṃ dṛḍhābaṃdhaṃ sucakrarathakūbaram .. 41 ..
4.134.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
सुविचित्रं चित्रतनुं श्रेष्ठकाष्ठमयं रथम् ॥
सुदृढाक्षं दृढाबंधं सुचक्ररथकूबरम् ॥ 41 ॥

4.134.s:
atha vā vaṃśavihitaṃ netrapaṭṭapaṭāvṛtam ..
tārakāśatacitrāṃśaṃ puṣpamālāvibhūṣitam .. 42 ..
4.134.d:
अथ वा वंशविहितं नेत्रपट्टपटावृतम् ॥
तारकाशतचित्रांशं पुष्पमालाविभूषितम् ॥ 42 ॥
4.134.m:
or else made of bamboo, covered with fine silk cloth,
patterned with hundreds of stars, and adorned with flower garlands;

4.134.s:
sitagoyugasaṃyuktaṃ pañcabāṇapatākinam ..
chatracāmaraśobhāḍhyaṃ sthāpayedbhavanāṅgaṇe .. 43 ..
4.134.d:
सितगोयुगसंयुक्तं पञ्चबाणपताकिनम् ॥
छत्रचामरशोभाढ्यं स्थापयेद्भवनाङ्गणे ॥ 43 ॥
4.134.m:
yoked with a pair of white cattle, bearing the banner of the Five-Arrowed One,
richly adorned with royal parasols and chowries, one should set it up in the courtyard of the house.

4.134.s:
vaiśvadevaṃ tataḥ kuryādgrahayajñavidhānataḥ ..
catuścaraṇakairmaṃtrairvipra śāntikapauṣṭikaiḥ .. 44 ..
4.134.d:
वैश्वदेवं ततः कुर्याद्ग्रहयज्ञविधानतः ॥
चतुश्चरणकैर्मंत्रैर्विप्र शान्तिकपौष्टिकैः ॥ 44 ॥
4.134.m:
Then, O Brahmin, one should perform the Vaiśvadeva rite according to the rule of the planetary sacrifice,
with four-footed mantras that bring peace and prosperity.

4.134.s:
āropayedrathe devaṃ mūlamaṃtreṇa maṃtravit ..
vedoktairathapaurāṇairgaṃdhadhūpādhivāsite .. 45 ..
4.134.d:
आरोपयेद्रथे देवं मूलमंत्रेण मंत्रवित् ॥
वेदोक्तैरथपौराणैर्गंधधूपाधिवासिते ॥ 45 ॥
4.134.m: The knower of mantras should place the god onto the chariot with the root mantra, / [and] with Vedic and Purāṇic [mantras], when it has been fumigated with fragrant incenses.

4.134.s:
rathe tiṣṭhannayati vājinaḥ puro yatrayatra kāmayate suṣārathiḥ ..
abhīṣūṇāṃ mahimānaṃ panāyata manuḥ paścādanuyacchanti raśmayaḥ..
śaṃkhaduṃdubhinirghoṣaiḥ kāhalānāṃ ca niḥsvanaiḥ..
hastadīpaiḥ prajvalitaistālakolāhā lena ca .. 47 ..
4.134.d:
रथे तिष्ठन्नयति वाजिनः पुरो यत्रयत्र कामयते सुषारथिः ॥
अभीषूणां महिमानं पनायत मनुः पश्चादनुयच्छन्ति रश्मयः॥
शंखदुंदुभिनिर्घोषैः काहलानां च निःस्वनैः॥
हस्तदीपैः प्रज्वलितैस्तालकोलाहा लेन च ॥ 47 ॥
4.134.m: Standing in the chariot, the skilled charioteer leads the horses forward wherever he desires; / praise the greatness of the reins, the mantra [says], and the rays follow behind. / With the roaring sounds of conchs and war drums, with the blasts of trumpets, / with burning hand-held torches, and with the clamour of cymbals,

4.134.s:
doṣāsukhena ramitaṃ preṣaṇīyapuraḥsaram ..
mahatotsavabhāreṇa bhrāmayetparito ratham..48..
4.134.d:
दोषासुखेन रमितं प्रेषणीयपुरःसरम् ॥
महतोत्सवभारेण भ्रामयेत्परितो रथम्॥48॥
4.134.m: delighted with nocturnal pleasure, preceded by theatrical troupes, / he should drive the chariot all around with the weight of a great festival.

4.134.s:
tāṃbūlāni rathe dadyātpuṣpamālāyutāni ca ..
rathavoḍhraṃ pradadyāttu prekṣakebhyo'pyavāritam .. 49 ..
4.134.d:
तांबूलानि रथे दद्यात्पुष्पमालायुतानि च ॥
रथवोढ्रं प्रदद्यात्तु प्रेक्षकेभ्योऽप्यवारितम् ॥ 49 ॥
4.134.m: He should present betels in the chariot, together with garlands of flowers; / he should also give [them] without hindrance to the chariot-drawers and to the onlookers.

4.134.s:
yasyayasya gṛhebhyeti prerito rathinā rathaḥ..
tasya tasya bhavetpūjyaḥ puṣpadhūpākṣatādibhiḥ ... .. 4.134.50 ..
4.134.d:
यस्ययस्य गृहेभ्येति प्रेरितो रथिना रथः॥
तस्य तस्य भवेत्पूज्यः पुष्पधूपाक्षतादिभिः ॥॥। 4.134.50 ॥
4.134.m: To whichever house the chariot, impelled by the charioteer, approaches, / by him it must be worshipped with flowers, incenses, unbroken grains, and the like.

4.134.s:
itaro'pi bhavetpūjyaḥ saṃprāpte gṛhiṇāṃ gṛhe ..
kiṃ punarjagatāṃ bhartā sarvalokamaheśvaraḥ .. 51 ..
4.134.d:
इतरोऽपि भवेत्पूज्यः संप्राप्ते गृहिणां गृहे ॥
किं पुनर्जगतां भर्ता सर्वलोकमहेश्वरः ॥ 51 ॥
4.134.m: Even an ordinary person must be honoured when he arrives at the house of householders; / how much more so the lord of the worlds, the supreme lord of all the worlds?

4.134.s:
kadācidakṣabhaṅgaḥ syāddhvajabhaṃgo'tha vā bhavet..
bhajyeta vā yugamadhye nahanaṃ truṭyate yadi .. 52 ..
4.134.d:
कदाचिदक्षभङ्गः स्याद्ध्वजभंगोऽथ वा भवेत्॥
भज्येत वा युगमध्ये नहनं त्रुट्यते यदि ॥ 52 ॥
4.134.m: If at any time an axle should break, or the banner should break, / or if [the chariot] should break in the middle of the yoke, or the fastening tear,

4.134.s:
brāhmaṇāṃstatra saṃpūjya homaḥ kāryo vijānatā ..
tilairājyena payasā yena saṃpadyate sukham .. .. 53 ..
4.134.d:
ब्राह्मणांस्तत्र संपूज्य होमः कार्यो विजानता ॥
तिलैराज्येन पयसा येन संपद्यते सुखम् ॥ ॥ 53 ॥
4.134.m: having worshipped the brāhmaṇas there, an oblation should be made by one who understands, / with sesamum, clarified butter, and milk, so that well-being may be attained.

4.134.s:
preraṇīprekṣaṇīyaiśca bhrāmayitvā rathottamam ..
sthāpayennagarasyāṃtastatra kuryānmahotsavam .. 54 ..
4.134.d:
प्रेरणीप्रेक्षणीयैश्च भ्रामयित्वा रथोत्तमम् ॥
स्थापयेन्नगरस्यांतस्तत्र कुर्यान्महोत्सवम् ॥ 54 ॥
4.134.m: Having driven the excellent chariot around with performers and spectacles, / he should station it inside the city, and perform a great festival there.

4.134.s:
dolāgrāhaiścakradolābhramairḍamarakaistathā ..
vidyādharīṇāṃ caritamitarābhiḥ prakāśyate .. 55 ..
4.134.d:
दोलाग्राहैश्चक्रदोलाभ्रमैर्डमरकैस्तथा ॥
विद्याधरीणां चरितमितराभिः प्रकाश्यते ॥ 55 ॥
4.134.m: With swing-seats, rotating Ferris wheels, and damarus, / the deeds of Vidyādharīs are displayed by other women.

4.134.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute pārtha sukhadaṃ tu rathotsavam ..
tathaiva pūjayetpārtha upavāsaparo naraḥ .. 56 ...
4.134.d:
एवं यः कुरुते पार्थ सुखदं तु रथोत्सवम् ॥
तथैव पूजयेत्पार्थ उपवासपरो नरः ॥ 56 ॥।
4.134.m: Whoever performs in this way, O Pārtha, this chariot-festival that grants happiness, / and in that very way, O Pārtha, a man intent on fasting worships,

4.134.s:
sarvavyādhivihīnaśca sukhī syāccharadāṃ śatam ..
yaḥ kārayitvā sauvarṇaṃ raupyaṃ vā rathamuttamam .. 57 ..
4.134.d:
सर्वव्याधिविहीनश्च सुखी स्याच्छरदां शतम् ॥
यः कारयित्वा सौवर्णं रौप्यं वा रथमुत्तमम् ॥ 57 ॥
4.134.m: he becomes free of all diseases and happy for a hundred autumns. / He who, having had an excellent chariot made of gold or silver,

4.134.s:
varṇakaiścitritaṃ divyaṃ dārujaṃ vā suśobhanam..
svahastaracitaṃ yaśca bhāskarāya nivedayet .. 58 ..
4.134.d:
वर्णकैश्चित्रितं दिव्यं दारुजं वा सुशोभनम्॥
स्वहस्तरचितं यश्च भास्कराय निवेदयेत् ॥ 58 ॥
4.134.m: or a divine one painted with pigments, or a very beautiful wooden one, / crafted with his own hands, presents it to the Sun,

4.134.s:
sa martyaloke sucirātsukhāni ca samaśnute ..
pūrvoktavidhinā bhānuṃ bhrāmayitvā rathe sthitam .. .. 59 ..
4.134.d:
स मर्त्यलोके सुचिरात्सुखानि च समश्नुते ॥
पूर्वोक्तविधिना भानुं भ्रामयित्वा रथे स्थितम् ॥ ॥ 59 ॥
4.134.m: enjoys pleasures for a very long time in the world of mortals. / Having driven the Sun stationed in the chariot in the manner stated before,

4.134.s:
sthāpayetsarvabhāge tu geyaṃ vādyapuraḥsaram ..
dakṣiṇe tu diśo bhāge dvitīye'hni nayedratham .. 4.134.60 ..
4.134.d:
स्थापयेत्सर्वभागे तु गेयं वाद्यपुरःसरम् ॥
दक्षिणे तु दिशो भागे द्वितीयेऽह्नि नयेद्रथम् ॥ 4.134.60 ॥
4.134.m: he should station it on every side, preceded by singing and instrumental music; / and on the second day he should take the chariot to the southern quarter.

4.134.s:
tatrāpi jāgaraṃ kuryādvādyagītasumaṃ galaiḥ ..
aparāyāṃ tṛtīye'hni sthāpayedrathamuttamam .. 61 ..
4.134.d:
तत्रापि जागरं कुर्याद्वाद्यगीतसुमं गलैः ॥
अपरायां तृतीयेऽह्नि स्थापयेद्रथमुत्तमम् ॥ 61 ॥
4.134.m: There too he should keep a vigil with auspicious instrumental music and songs; / on the third day he should station the excellent chariot in the western [quarter].

4.134.s:
prekṣaṇīyavinodena tāṃ rātrimativāhayet ..
sthāpayeduttarasyāṃ tu caturthe divase ratham .. ..62 ..
4.134.d:
प्रेक्षणीयविनोदेन तां रात्रिमतिवाहयेत् ॥
स्थापयेदुत्तरस्यां तु चतुर्थे दिवसे रथम् ॥ ॥62 ॥
4.134.m: He should pass that night with the diversion of theatrical spectacles; / and on the fourth day he should station the chariot in the northern [quarter].

4.134.s:
mahāyātrāṃ prakurvīta tatrāpyadbhutaceṣṭitam ..
paṃcame divase prāpte nagarāṃtasthitaṃ ravim .. 63
4.134.d:
महायात्रां प्रकुर्वीत तत्राप्यद्भुतचेष्टितम् ॥
पंचमे दिवसे प्राप्ते नगरांतस्थितं रविम् ॥ 63
4.134.m: He should perform a great procession, wonderful in its actions, there too; / when the fifth day has arrived, [for] the Sun stationed at the edge of the city,

4.134.s:
pūjayitvā vidhānena ṣaṣṭhe'hni bhavanaṃ nayet ..
rathayātrāprasaṃgena kathitā rathasaptamī .. 64 ..
4.134.d:
पूजयित्वा विधानेन षष्ठेऽह्नि भवनं नयेत् ॥
रथयात्राप्रसंगेन कथिता रथसप्तमी ॥ 64 ॥
4.134.m: having worshipped him according to the rules, he should bring him home on the sixth day. / In connection with the chariot procession, Rathasaptamī has been spoken of.

4.134.s:
sarvapāpaharā puṇyā kiñcidanyannibodha me ..
gaurī pūjyā tṛtīyāyāṃ caturthyāṃ vighnanāyakaḥ .. 65 ..
4.134.d:
सर्वपापहरा पुण्या किञ्चिदन्यन्निबोध मे ॥
गौरी पूज्या तृतीयायां चतुर्थ्यां विघ्ननायकः ॥ 65 ॥
4.134.m: It removes all sins and is holy. Learn something else from me: / Gaurī is to be worshipped on the third [lunar day], and the leader of obstacles on the fourth.

4.134.s:
pañcamyāṃ paṃkajakarāṃ pūjayedvā sarasvatīm ..
ṣaṣṭhyāṃ śaktidharaṃ skandaṃ saptamyāṃ tu divākaram .. 66 ..
4.134.d:
पञ्चम्यां पंकजकरां पूजयेद्वा सरस्वतीम् ॥
षष्ठ्यां शक्तिधरं स्कन्दं सप्तम्यां तु दिवाकरम् ॥ 66 ॥
4.134.m: On the fifth he should worship the lotus-handed Sarasvatī; / on the sixth, Skanda who bears the spear; and on the seventh, the Sun.

4.134.s:
aṣṭamyāṃ ca caturdaśyāṃ sampūjyaḥ śaśiśekharaḥ ..
navamyāṃ pūjayeccaṇḍīṃ cāmuṇḍāṃ muṇḍamālinīm .. 67 ..
4.134.d:
अष्टम्यां च चतुर्दश्यां सम्पूज्यः शशिशेखरः ॥
नवम्यां पूजयेच्चण्डीं चामुण्डां मुण्डमालिनीम् ॥ 67 ॥
4.134.m: On the eighth and on the fourteenth, the Moon-crested Lord is to be worshipped; / on the ninth he should worship Caṇḍī, Cāmuṇḍā, garlanded with severed heads.

4.134.s:
daśamyāmṛṣayaḥ śāṃtāḥ sarve vyāsapurassarāḥ ..
ekādaśyāṃ cakrapāṇiṃ dvādaśyāṃ vā samarcayet..68..
4.134.d:
दशम्यामृषयः शांताः सर्वे व्यासपुरस्सराः ॥
एकादश्यां चक्रपाणिं द्वादश्यां वा समर्चयेत्॥68॥
4.134.m: On the tenth, the tranquil sages, all headed by Vyāsa, [are to be worshipped]; / on the eleventh or on the twelfth he should worship the Discus-handed Lord.

4.134.s:
trayodaśyāṃ trinetrotthavahninā śāṃtavigraham..
sādhāraṇī tu sarveṣāṃ paurṇamāsī tithiḥ smṛtā..69..
4.134.d:
त्रयोदश्यां त्रिनेत्रोत्थवह्निना शांतविग्रहम्॥
साधारणी तु सर्वेषां पौर्णमासी तिथिः स्मृता॥69॥
4.134.m: On the thirteenth, him whose form was pacified by the fire arising from the Three-Eyed Lord [is to be worshipped]; / and the full moon day is considered common to all.

4.134.s:
āṃdolake madanake rathayātrāsu caiva hi..
vyutkrameṇāpi kartavyā tithīnāṃ kāryagauravāt..
yātrā vāsaṃtikī ceyaṃ cittasvāsthyakarī parā..4.134.70..
4.134.d:
आंदोलके मदनके रथयात्रासु चैव हि॥
व्युत्क्रमेणापि कर्तव्या तिथीनां कार्यगौरवात्॥
यात्रा वासंतिकी चेयं चित्तस्वास्थ्यकरी परा॥4.134.70॥
4.134.m: In swing rites, Madana rites, and in chariot processions, / [the worship] may be performed even out of order, on account of the importance of the rite among the lunar days; / and this vernal procession is supreme, producing peace of mind.

4.134.s:
samyaksudhādhavalite bhavane surāṇāmaṃtassuvastramaṇimauktikadānacitre ..
tāṃbūlakakramukavāravilāsinībhiryātrāṃ vidhāya bhavatīha sa bhārateśaḥ .. .. 71 .. ..
madanamahotsavavarṇanam
4.134.d:
सम्यक्सुधाधवलिते भवने सुराणामंतस्सुवस्त्रमणिमौक्तिकदानचित्रे ॥
तांबूलकक्रमुकवारविलासिनीभिर्यात्रां विधाय भवतीह स भारतेशः ॥ ॥ 71 ॥ ॥
मदनमहोत्सववर्णनम्
4.134.m:
Having celebrated the procession in the temple of the gods, properly whitened with lime, decorated within by gifts of fine clothes, gems, and pearls, with betel, areca nuts, and courtesans, he becomes a lord of Bhārata in this world.
Description of the Great Festival of Madana

4.135.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
gaurīṃ vivāhya jagrāha haraḥ pāśupataṃ vratam ..
umāpatiḥ paśupatirdhyānāsakto babhūva ha .. 1 ..
4.135.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
गौरीं विवाह्य जग्राह हरः पाशुपतं व्रतम् ॥
उमापतिः पशुपतिर्ध्यानासक्तो बभूव ह ॥ 1 ॥
4.135.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / Having married Gaurī, Hara took up the Pāśupata observance; / the husband of Umā, the Lord of Beasts, became absorbed in meditation.

4.135.s:
brahmādibhiḥ samāmaṃtrya vibudhaiḥ putralabdhaye ..
gauryā manobhilaṣitapūraṇāya praharṣitaiḥ .. 2 ..
4.135.d:
ब्रह्मादिभिः समामंत्र्य विबुधैः पुत्रलब्धये ॥
गौर्या मनोभिलषितपूरणाय प्रहर्षितैः ॥ 2 ॥
4.135.m: Having deliberated, the gods headed by Brahmā, rejoiced, / in order to obtain a son and to fulfil Gaurī’s heart's desire,

4.135.s:
prahitaḥ kṣobhaṇārthāya samartha iti manmathaḥ..
tato māraḥ smaraḥ kāmopyājagāma tamāśramam .. 3 ..
4.135.d:
प्रहितः क्षोभणार्थाय समर्थ इति मन्मथः॥
ततो मारः स्मरः कामोप्याजगाम तमाश्रमम् ॥ 3 ॥
4.135.m: dispatched Manmatha, [thinking] he was capable, in order to agitate [him]; / then Māra, Smara, who is Kāma, went to that hermitage,

4.135.s:
ratiprītimadonmādavasaṃtaśrīsahāyavān ..
nidhānavāruṇīdarpaśṛṃgāraiḥ parivāritaḥ .. 4 ..
4.135.d:
रतिप्रीतिमदोन्मादवसंतश्रीसहायवान् ॥
निधानवारुणीदर्पशृंगारैः परिवारितः ॥ 4 ॥
4.135.m: accompanied by Rati, Prīti, Mada, Unmāda, Spring, and Śrī; / surrounded by treasures, Vāruṇī, pride, and erotic passion;

4.135.s:
āmrāśokavanottaṃso mālatīkṛtaśekharaḥ ..
vīṇāmṛdaṃgasaṃgītakokilāśṛṃgadūtakaḥ ..5..
4.135.d:
आम्राशोकवनोत्तंसो मालतीकृतशेखरः ॥
वीणामृदंगसंगीतकोकिलाशृंगदूतकः ॥5॥
4.135.m: with an ear-ornament of mango and aśoka groves, wearing a crest of jasmine flowers, / with lutes, mṛdaṅga drums, music, cuckoos, and horn-[trumpets] as his messengers;

4.135.s:
jhallarīvādyasaṃghuṣṭabhāṃḍāgārikalekhakaḥ ..
pānamattāṅganārūḍho hindolāścaryamaṃtrimān .. 6 ..
4.135.d:
झल्लरीवाद्यसंघुष्टभांडागारिकलेखकः ॥
पानमत्ताङ्गनारूढो हिन्दोलाश्चर्यमंत्रिमान् ॥ 6 ॥
4.135.m: with a treasurer and a scribe proclaimed by the playing of jhallarī cymbals, / mounted on a woman intoxicated with drink, possessing marvellous ministers for the swing;

4.135.s:
dakṣiṇānilagaṃdhāḍhyaḥ kaṭākṣekṣitavarṣavān ..
mahārājādhirājo vā smaraḥ prāpto harāṃtikam .. 7 ..
4.135.d:
दक्षिणानिलगंधाढ्यः कटाक्षेक्षितवर्षवान् ॥
महाराजाधिराजो वा स्मरः प्राप्तो हरांतिकम् ॥ 7 ॥
4.135.m: rich in the fragrance of the southern wind, showering side-glances, / like a great emperor of kings, Smara arrived near Hara.

4.135.s:
sa puṣpacāpamākṛṣya madanonmādanaṃ śaram ..
cikṣepa tripuraghnāya samādherbhaṃgahetave .. 8 ..
4.135.d:
स पुष्पचापमाकृष्य मदनोन्मादनं शरम् ॥
चिक्षेप त्रिपुरघ्नाय समाधेर्भंगहेतवे ॥ 8 ॥
4.135.m: Drawing his flower-bow, he shot the arrow that intoxicates with passion / at the destroyer of Tripura, for the sake of breaking his meditation.

4.135.s:
buddhvā taṃ tasya saṃkalpaṃ rudraḥ krodhājjvalanruṣā ..
lalāṭādvahnimasṛjattṛtīya nayanāddharaḥ .. 9 ..
4.135.d:
बुद्ध्वा तं तस्य संकल्पं रुद्रः क्रोधाज्ज्वलन्रुषा ॥
ललाटाद्वह्निमसृजत्तृतीय नयनाद्धरः ॥ 9 ॥
4.135.m: Perceiving that intention of his, Rudra, blazing in fury from anger, / released fire from his forehead, from his third eye, [did] Hara.

4.135.s:
kāmo vilokitastena bhasmībhūtaśca tatkṣaṇāt ..
dagdhaṃ dṛṣṭvā smaraṃ śokādratiprītī sthite sadā .. 4.135.10 ..
4.135.d:
कामो विलोकितस्तेन भस्मीभूतश्च तत्क्षणात् ॥
दग्धं दृष्ट्वा स्मरं शोकाद्रतिप्रीती स्थिते सदा ॥ 4.135.10 ॥
4.135.m: Kāma was looked upon by him and was turned to ashes that very instant; / seeing Smara burned, Rati and Prīti stood constantly in grief,

4.135.s:
karuṇaṃ vilapaṃtyau te sarvamanyaddiśaṃ gatam ..
tataḥ śokārtahṛdayā gaurī rudramuvāca ha .. 11 ..
4.135.d:
करुणं विलपंत्यौ ते सर्वमन्यद्दिशं गतम् ॥
ततः शोकार्तहृदया गौरी रुद्रमुवाच ह ॥ 11 ॥
4.135.m: lamenting piteously, while everyone else fled in every direction. / Then, her heart afflicted with sorrow, Gaurī spoke to Rudra:

4.135.s:
bhagavannasmadarthe taṃ kāmaṃ nirdagdhavānasi ..
tenaite paśya nāryau te kāmasya ruditaḥ katham .. 12 ..
4.135.d:
भगवन्नस्मदर्थे तं कामं निर्दग्धवानसि ॥
तेनैते पश्य नार्यौ ते कामस्य रुदितः कथम् ॥ 12 ॥
4.135.m: “O Blessed One, for our sake you burnt Kāma to ashes; / therefore, look at these two women of Kāma, how they weep!

4.135.s:
kuru prasādaṃ deveśa ratiprītye vṛṣadhvaja ..
saṃjīvaya smaraṃ śaṃbho mūrtimaṃtaṃ punaḥ kuru .. 13 ..
4.135.d:
कुरु प्रसादं देवेश रतिप्रीत्ये वृषध्वज ॥
संजीवय स्मरं शंभो मूर्तिमंतं पुनः कुरु ॥ 13 ॥
4.135.m: Grant your favour, O Lord of gods, O bull-bannered Lord, for the sake of Rati and Prīti; / revive Smara, O Śambhu, make him embodied once again!”

4.135.s:
tacchrutvā tu mahādevo hṛṣṭaḥ provāca pārvatīm ..
upaplutaṃ jagatsarvaṃ manmathena śarīriṇā .. 14 ..
4.135.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा तु महादेवो हृष्टः प्रोवाच पार्वतीम् ॥
उपप्लुतं जगत्सर्वं मन्मथेन शरीरिणा ॥ 14 ॥
4.135.m: Having heard that, Mahādeva, delighted, said to Pārvatī: / “The entire world was harassed by Manmatha when he had a body.

4.135.s:
mayā dagdhasya kāmasya punarāgamanaṃ kutaḥ ..
kiṃ tu te mānayanvākyaṃ karomi saphalaṃ priye..15 ..
4.135.d:
मया दग्धस्य कामस्य पुनरागमनं कुतः ॥
किं तु ते मानयन्वाक्यं करोमि सफलं प्रिये॥15 ॥
4.135.m: Whence can there be a return of Kāma who was burned by me? / Yet, respecting your words, I shall make them fruitful, my beloved.

4.135.s:
asminvasaṃtasamaye śuklapakṣe trayodaśī ..
asyāṃ manobhavo devi bhaviṣyati śarīravān .. 16 ..
4.135.d:
अस्मिन्वसंतसमये शुक्लपक्षे त्रयोदशी ॥
अस्यां मनोभवो देवि भविष्यति शरीरवान् ॥ 16 ॥
4.135.m: In this spring season, on the thirteenth [tithi] of the bright fortnight, / on this day, O goddess, the Mind-born one will become embodied.

4.135.s:
etena bījabhūtena jagadvarṇiṣyate'khilam ..
evaṃ varamimaṃ dattvā manmathāya yudhiṣṭhira ..17..
4.135.d:
एतेन बीजभूतेन जगद्वर्णिष्यतेऽखिलम् ॥
एवं वरमिमं दत्त्वा मन्मथाय युधिष्ठिर ॥17॥
4.135.m: With him as the seed-source, the entire world will be populated.' / Having given this boon to Manmatha in this way, O Yudhiṣṭhira,

4.135.s:
jagāma himavacchṛṃgaṃ kailāsaṃ pārvatīpriyaḥ ..
tadetatsarvamākhyātaṃ smarasya caritaṃ nṛpa .. 18 ..
4.135.d:
जगाम हिमवच्छृंगं कैलासं पार्वतीप्रियः ॥
तदेतत्सर्वमाख्यातं स्मरस्य चरितं नृप ॥ 18 ॥
4.135.m: the lover of Pārvatī went to Kailāsa, a peak of the Himavat. / Thus all this deed of Smara has been told, O king.

4.135.s:
pūjāvidhānamaparaṃ kathayāmi śṛṇuṇva tat ..
asyāṃ snātvā trayodaśyāmaśokākhyaṃ nagaṃ likhet .. 19 ..
4.135.d:
पूजाविधानमपरं कथयामि शृणुण्व तत् ॥
अस्यां स्नात्वा त्रयोदश्यामशोकाख्यं नगं लिखेत् ॥ 19 ॥
4.135.m: I shall tell you another rule of worship; listen to it. / Having bathed on this thirteenth [tithi], one should draw the tree named aśoka;

4.135.s:
sindūrajanitairaṃgairatiprīti samanvitam .
kāmadevaṃ vasaṃtaṃ ca vājivaktraṃ jhaṣadhvajam .. 4.135.20 ..
4.135.d:
सिन्दूरजनितैरंगैरतिप्रीति समन्वितम् ।
कामदेवं वसंतं च वाजिवक्त्रं झषध्वजम् ॥ 4.135.20 ॥
4.135.m: with limbs created from vermilion, full of great affection, / [and draw] Kāmadeva and spring, horse-faced and with a fish-banner,

4.135.s:
sauvarṇaṃ vā mahārāja vārkṣaṃ citramathāpi vā ..
līlāvilāsagamanaṃ garvitaṃ sāpsa rogaṇam ..21..
4.135.d:
सौवर्णं वा महाराज वार्क्षं चित्रमथापि वा ॥
लीलाविलासगमनं गर्वितं साप्स रोगणम् ॥21॥
4.135.m: or golden, O great king, wooden, or even painted, / moving with playful grace, proud, accompanied by a host of apsarases,

4.135.s:
gandharvagītavāditraprekṣaṇīyasamākulam ..
naṃdyāvartiratikrīḍāprītividyādharairyutam ..22..
4.135.d:
गन्धर्वगीतवादित्रप्रेक्षणीयसमाकुलम् ॥
नंद्यावर्तिरतिक्रीडाप्रीतिविद्याधरैर्युतम् ॥22॥
4.135.m: crowded with gandharva songs, instrumental music, and dramatic spectacles, / and joined by Vidyādharas delighted with joyful play [like] the nandyāvarta.

4.135.s:
madhyāhne bhojayedbhaktyā bhakṣyairdhūpaiḥsragaṃbaraiḥ..
maṃtreṇānena kauṃteya naro nāryā samanvitaḥ .. 23 ..
4.135.d:
मध्याह्ने भोजयेद्भक्त्या भक्ष्यैर्धूपैःस्रगंबरैः॥
मंत्रेणानेन कौंतेय नरो नार्या समन्वितः ॥ 23 ॥
4.135.m: At midday, a man accompanied by his wife should worship [him] with devotion, / with sweets, incenses, garlands, and garments, using this mantra, O son of Kuntī:

4.135.s:
namo vāmāya kāmāya devadevāya mūrtaye ..
brahmaviṣṇuśivendrāṇāṃ manaḥkṣobhakarāya vai .. 24 ..
4.135.d:
नमो वामाय कामाय देवदेवाय मूर्तये ॥
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवेन्द्राणां मनःक्षोभकराय वै ॥ 24 ॥
4.135.m: 'Obeisance to Vāma, to Kāma, to the god of gods, to the embodied form, / indeed to the one who agitates the minds of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and Indra.'

4.135.s:
kṛtvaivamarcayitvā tu devadevamanobhavam ..
tatastasyāgrato deyā modakā mukhamodakāḥ .. 25 ..
4.135.d:
कृत्वैवमर्चयित्वा तु देवदेवमनोभवम् ॥
ततस्तस्याग्रतो देया मोदका मुखमोदकाः ॥ 25 ॥
4.135.m: Having thus worshipped the Mind-born god of gods, / modakas that delight the mouth should then be offered before him,

4.135.s:
nānāprakārānbhakṣyāṃśca kāmo me prīyatāmiti ..
tato visarjayedviprāndattvā yugmaṃ sadakṣiṇam .. 26 ..
4.135.d:
नानाप्रकारान्भक्ष्यांश्च कामो मे प्रीयतामिति ॥
ततो विसर्जयेद्विप्रान्दत्त्वा युग्मं सदक्षिणम् ॥ 26 ॥
4.135.m: and various kinds of food, saying: 'May Kāma be pleased with me.' / Then he should dismiss the brāhmaṇas after giving [them] a pair [of garments] with a fee.

4.135.s:
svapatiṃ pūjayennārī vastramālāvibhūṣaṇaiḥ ..
kāmo'yamiti saṃciṃtya prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā ..27..
4.135.d:
स्वपतिं पूजयेन्नारी वस्त्रमालाविभूषणैः ॥
कामोऽयमिति संचिंत्य प्रहृष्टेनांतरात्मना ॥27॥
4.135.m: A woman should worship her own husband with garments, garlands, and ornaments, / with a delighted inner self, thinking: 'He is Kāma.'

4.135.s:
manmathāyatane tasminyajamānaḥ suhṛdvṛtaḥ ..
rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kuryātsukharātriryathā bhavet .. 28 ..
4.135.d:
मन्मथायतने तस्मिन्यजमानः सुहृद्वृतः ॥
रात्रौ जागरणं कुर्यात्सुखरात्रिर्यथा भवेत् ॥ 28 ॥
4.135.m: In that temple of Manmatha, the sacrificer, surrounded by friends, / should keep vigil at night so that it becomes a night of happiness.

4.135.s:
karpūrakuṃkumakṣodagaṃdhatāṃbūlasarjanaiḥ ..
nānāprakārairbhakṣyaiśca kuryādrātrau mahotsavam .. 29 ..
4.135.d:
कर्पूरकुंकुमक्षोदगंधतांबूलसर्जनैः ॥
नानाप्रकारैर्भक्ष्यैश्च कुर्याद्रात्रौ महोत्सवम् ॥ 29 ॥
4.135.m: With camphor, saffron powder, fragrances, and gifts of betel, / and with various kinds of foods, he should hold a great festival at night,

4.135.s:
dīpaprajvālanairnṛtyaiḥ prekṣaṇaiḥ prekṣaṇotsavaiḥ ..
evaṃ yaḥ kurute pārtha varṣevarṣe mahotsavam .. 4.135.30 ..
4.135.d:
दीपप्रज्वालनैर्नृत्यैः प्रेक्षणैः प्रेक्षणोत्सवैः ॥
एवं यः कुरुते पार्थ वर्षेवर्षे महोत्सवम् ॥ 4.135.30 ॥
4.135.m: with lighting of lamps, dances, theatrical shows, and festive spectacles. / A king in his city who thus celebrates this great festival year after year, O son of Pṛthā,

4.135.s:
vasaṃtasamaye prāpte hṛṣṭastuṣṭo nṛpaḥ pure ..
tasya saṃvatsaraṃ yāvalloko rogairvimucyate .. 31 ..
4.135.d:
वसंतसमये प्राप्ते हृष्टस्तुष्टो नृपः पुरे ॥
तस्य संवत्सरं यावल्लोको रोगैर्विमुच्यते ॥ 31 ॥
4.135.m: delighted and content when the spring season has arrived— / for a whole year his people are freed from diseases;

4.135.s:
subhikṣaṃ kṣemamārogyaṃ yaśaḥ śrīḥ saukhyamuttamam ..
kāmavarṣī ca parjanyastasminrāṣṭre prajāyate .. 32 ..
4.135.d:
सुभिक्षं क्षेममारोग्यं यशः श्रीः सौख्यमुत्तमम् ॥
कामवर्षी च पर्जन्यस्तस्मिन्राष्ट्रे प्रजायते ॥ 32 ॥
4.135.m: plenty, welfare, health, fame, prosperity, and supreme happiness [abound], / and rain pouring down according to desire occurs in that realm.

4.135.s:
tuṣyate tu bhṛśaṃ devo dvādaśārddhārddhalocanaḥ ..
tathā kāmaśca viṣṇuśca vasaṃtaśca prajāpatiḥ .. 33..
4.135.d:
तुष्यते तु भृशं देवो द्वादशार्द्धार्द्धलोचनः ॥
तथा कामश्च विष्णुश्च वसंतश्च प्रजापतिः ॥ 33॥
4.135.m: The god with twelve-and-a-half-half eyes is exceedingly pleased, / as are Kāma, Viṣṇu, spring, and Prajāpati;

4.135.s:
candrasūryādikā sarve grahā brahmarṣayastathā ..
sarve'pi tasya tuṣyaṃti yakṣagaṃdharvadānavāḥ .. 34 ..
4.135.d:
चन्द्रसूर्यादिका सर्वे ग्रहा ब्रह्मर्षयस्तथा ॥
सर्वेऽपि तस्य तुष्यंति यक्षगंधर्वदानवाः ॥ 34 ॥
4.135.m: all the planets beginning with the moon and the sun, and the celestial seers, / all the yakṣas, gandharvas, and dānavas are also pleased with him;

4.135.s:
asurā yātudhānāśca suparṇāḥ patagā nagāḥ ..
tuṣṭāḥ prayacchaṃti sukhaṃ tasya karturna saṃśayaḥ .. 35 ..
4.135.d:
असुरा यातुधानाश्च सुपर्णाः पतगा नगाः ॥
तुष्टाः प्रयच्छंति सुखं तस्य कर्तुर्न संशयः ॥ 35 ॥
4.135.m: the asuras, yātudhānas, suparṇas, birds, and mountains, / pleased, grant happiness to the performer of that [festival], without doubt.

4.135.s:
caitrotsave sakalalokamanonivāsaṃ kāmaṃ vasaṃtamalayādrimarutsahāyam ..
ratyā sahārcya puruṣaḥ pravarā ca yoṣitsaubhāgyarūpasutasaukhyayutā sadā syāt .. 36 ..
bhūtamātryutsavavarṇanam
4.135.d:
चैत्रोत्सवे सकललोकमनोनिवासं कामं वसंतमलयाद्रिमरुत्सहायम् ॥
रत्या सहार्च्य पुरुषः प्रवरा च योषित्सौभाग्यरूपसुतसौख्ययुता सदा स्यात् ॥ 36 ॥
भूतमात्र्युत्सववर्णनम्
4.135.m:
Having worshipped Kāma, who abides in the minds of all beings, / whose companions are spring and the wind from the Malaya mountains, / along with Rati during the spring festival, a man and an excellent woman / will always be endowed with good fortune, beauty, sons, and happiness.
Description of the Festival of Bhūtamātā

4.136.s:
.. yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
bhūtamāteti saṃhṛṣṭe grāmegrāme purepure ..
gāyannṛtyanhasam̐llokaḥ sarvataḥ paridhāvati .. 1 ..
4.136.d:
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
भूतमातेति संहृष्टे ग्रामेग्रामे पुरेपुरे ॥
गायन्नृत्यन्हसम्̐ल्लोकः सर्वतः परिधावति ॥ 1 ॥
4.136.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / In every village and in every city, overjoyed [saying] 'Bhūtamātā!', / singing, dancing, and laughing, the people run around on all sides.

4.136.s:
unmattavatpralapati kṣitau patati mattavat ..
kruddhavaddhāvati purānmattavatkarṣate bahiḥ .. 2 ..
4.136.d:
उन्मत्तवत्प्रलपति क्षितौ पतति मत्तवत् ॥
क्रुद्धवद्धावति पुरान्मत्तवत्कर्षते बहिः ॥ 2 ॥
4.136.m: [A person] babbles like a madman, falls on the ground like one drunk, / runs from the city like one enraged, and drags [others] outside like one intoxicated.

4.136.s:
mukhāṃgabhaṃgānkurute loke vātagṛhītavat ..
bhūtavadbhasmagātraṃ tu kardamānavagāhate .. 3 ..
4.136.d:
मुखांगभंगान्कुरुते लोके वातगृहीतवत् ॥
भूतवद्भस्मगात्रं तु कर्दमानवगाहते ॥ 3 ॥
4.136.m: Among the folk, one makes contortions of the mouth and limbs like one seized by wind; / with body smeared with ashes like a ghost, one plunges into mud.

4.136.s:
kimeṣa śāstranirdiṣṭo mārgaḥ kimuta laukikaḥ ..
muhyate me manaḥ kṛṣṇa tvaṃ tu vaktumihārhasi .. 4 ..
4.136.d:
किमेष शास्त्रनिर्दिष्टो मार्गः किमुत लौकिकः ॥
मुह्यते मे मनः कृष्ण त्वं तु वक्तुमिहार्हसि ॥ 4 ॥
4.136.m: Is this a path enjoined by scripture, or is it worldly custom? / My mind is bewildered, O Kṛṣṇa; you ought to explain it here.

4.136.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu pārtha pravakṣyāmi yatte kiñcinmanogatam ..
āstikaḥ śraddadhānaśca bhavatīti matirmama .. 5 ..
4.136.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
शृणु पार्थ प्रवक्ष्यामि यत्ते किञ्चिन्मनोगतम् ॥
आस्तिकः श्रद्दधानश्च भवतीति मतिर्मम ॥ 5 ॥
4.136.m: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: / Listen, O son of Pṛthā; I shall tell you what is on your mind. / It is my thought that you are an orthodox believer and full of faith.

4.136.s:
pārvatyā sahitaḥ pārtha mandare cārukandare ..
krīḍannāste mudā yukto divyakrīḍanakairharaḥ .. 6 ..
4.136.d:
पार्वत्या सहितः पार्थ मन्दरे चारुकन्दरे ॥
क्रीडन्नास्ते मुदा युक्तो दिव्यक्रीडनकैर्हरः ॥ 6 ॥
4.136.m: Accompanied by Pārvatī, O son of Pṛthā, in a delightful cave on Mount Mandara, / Hara sat playing with delight using divine playthings.

4.136.s:
haṃsonnatagatiṃ cārukumbhabhrājikucadvayam ..
siñjatsadraśanāṃ hṛṣṭāṃ dṛṣṭvā gaurīṃ jagadguruḥ .. 7 ..
4.136.d:
हंसोन्नतगतिं चारुकुम्भभ्राजिकुचद्वयम् ॥
सिञ्जत्सद्रशनां हृष्टां दृष्ट्वा गौरीं जगद्गुरुः ॥ 7 ॥
4.136.m: Seeing Gaurī, whose gait was elevated like a swan's, / whose two breasts shone like lovely water-jars, / whose fine girdle jingled, and who was full of joy, the Guru of the universe,

4.136.s:
dagdhakāmo'pi ca haraḥ saṃdīptamadano'bhavat ..
niḥsṛtāṃ kāmayāmāsa mahārhaśayane śivaḥ .. 8 ..
4.136.d:
दग्धकामोऽपि च हरः संदीप्तमदनोऽभवत् ॥
निःसृतां कामयामास महार्हशयने शिवः ॥ 8 ॥
4.136.m: Hara, even though he had burned Kāma, had his desire rekindled. / Śiva desired her as she emerged on the costly couch.

4.136.s:
ratasthayostayorjātaṃ divyavarṣaśataṃ yadā ..
tadā devīsamucchrāyanirodhānnirgatā bahiḥ..9..
4.136.d:
रतस्थयोस्तयोर्जातं दिव्यवर्षशतं यदा ॥
तदा देवीसमुच्छ्रायनिरोधान्निर्गता बहिः॥9॥
4.136.m: When a hundred divine years had passed while the two were engaged in love-play, / she went outside due to the obstruction of the goddess's urine;

4.136.s:
mūtrodakātsamuttasthau nārī nirdāritodarā ..
kṛṣṇā karālavadanā piṃgākṣā muktamūrddhajā .. 4.136.10 ..
4.136.d:
मूत्रोदकात्समुत्तस्थौ नारी निर्दारितोदरा ॥
कृष्णा करालवदना पिंगाक्षा मुक्तमूर्द्धजा ॥ 4.136.10 ॥
4.136.m: from the urinary fluid there arose a woman whose belly was torn open, / dark, with a terrifying face, tawny-eyed, and with dishevelled hair,

4.136.s:
kapālamālābharaṇā baddhapiṃḍordhvapiṃḍikā ..
khaṭvāṅgakaṃ kāladharā mudrāṅkitakarā śivā .. 11 ..
4.136.d:
कपालमालाभरणा बद्धपिंडोर्ध्वपिंडिका ॥
खट्वाङ्गकं कालधरा मुद्राङ्कितकरा शिवा ॥ 11 ॥
4.136.m: adorned with a garland of skulls, with upper and lower lumps bound [about her], / bearing a khaṭvāṅga and a staff, her hands marked with mudrās, an auspicious [yet terrifying] goddess,

4.136.s:
vyāghracarmāṃbaradharā raṇatkiṃkiṇimekhalā ..
ḍamaḍḍamaḍḍamarukā phūtkārāpūritāṃbarā .. 12 ...
4.136.d:
व्याघ्रचर्मांबरधरा रणत्किंकिणिमेखला ॥
डमड्डमड्डमरुका फूत्कारापूरितांबरा ॥ 12 ॥।
4.136.m: wearing a garment of tiger-skin, with a girdle of jingling bells, / sounding 'ḍamaḍ-ḍamaḍ' on a ḍamaru, filling the sky with puffs of breath.

4.136.s:
tasyāḥ pārśvānujāścānyā gītavādyalayānugāḥ ..
uttālatālamabalā nṛtyaṃti ca hasaṃti ca .. 13 ..
4.136.d:
तस्याः पार्श्वानुजाश्चान्या गीतवाद्यलयानुगाः ॥
उत्तालतालमबला नृत्यंति च हसंति च ॥ 13 ॥
4.136.m: Her other female companions at her side, following the rhythm of songs and instruments, / keeping a high tempo, dance and laugh,

4.136.s:
kapālakhaṭvāṅgadharā gajacarmāvaguṇṭhitāḥ ..
tathaiva śaṃkarājjātastadrūpābharaṇaḥ pumān .. 14 ..
4.136.d:
कपालखट्वाङ्गधरा गजचर्मावगुण्ठिताः ॥
तथैव शंकराज्जातस्तद्रूपाभरणः पुमान् ॥ 14 ॥
4.136.m: holding skulls and khaṭvāṅgas, veiled in elephant hides. / In the very same way, a male was born from Śaṅkara, having the same appearance and ornaments,

4.136.s:
anugamyamāno bahubhirbhūtairatibhayaṃkaraiḥ ..
siṃhaśārdūlavadanai radanollikhitāṃbaraiḥ .. 15 ..
4.136.d:
अनुगम्यमानो बहुभिर्भूतैरतिभयंकरैः ॥
सिंहशार्दूलवदनै रदनोल्लिखितांबरैः ॥ 15 ॥
4.136.m: followed by many extremely terrifying bhūtas / with faces of lions and tigers, whose teeth scraped the sky.

4.136.s:
ekībhūtaiḥ kṣaṇenaiva tau bhavānībhavodbhavau ..
dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭamanā devaḥ prāha devīṃ suvismitām .. 16 ..
4.136.d:
एकीभूतैः क्षणेनैव तौ भवानीभवोद्भवौ ॥
दृष्ट्वा हृष्टमना देवः प्राह देवीं सुविस्मिताम् ॥ 16 ॥
4.136.m: Seeing those two born from Bhavānī and Bhava, united in a single moment, / the god, delighted in mind, spoke to the utterly astonished goddess:

4.136.s:
kalyāṇi paśya paśyaitau mattvadaṅgasamudbhavau ..
bībhatsādbhutaśṛṃgāravarāyudhavidhāriṇau .. 17 ..
4.136.d:
कल्याणि पश्य पश्यैतौ मत्त्वदङ्गसमुद्भवौ ॥
बीभत्साद्भुतशृंगारवरायुधविधारिणौ ॥ 17 ॥
4.136.m: 'O auspicious one, see, see these two sprung from your body and mine, / displaying the repulsive, wondrous, and erotic sentiments, and holding excellent weapons!

4.136.s:
bhrātṛbhāṃḍau yathā devi tadvadetau matau mama ..
nṛnāryoraṃtaraṃ kiñcitsādṛśyātpratibhāsayet .. 18 ..
4.136.d:
भ्रातृभांडौ यथा देवि तद्वदेतौ मतौ मम ॥
नृनार्योरंतरं किञ्चित्सादृश्यात्प्रतिभासयेत् ॥ 18 ॥
4.136.m: Just as they are brother and sister, O goddess, so are they regarded by me; / some slight distinction between male and female is made apparent by their resemblance.'

4.136.s:
bhrātṛbhāṃḍā bhūtamātā tathaivodakasevikā ..
saṃjñātrayaṃ tayoḥ kṛtvā tataḥ prādādvaraṃ haraḥ .. 19 ..
4.136.d:
भ्रातृभांडा भूतमाता तथैवोदकसेविका ॥
संज्ञात्रयं तयोः कृत्वा ततः प्रादाद्वरं हरः ॥ 19 ॥
4.136.m: Having given them three names: Bhrātṛbhāṇḍā, Bhūtamātā, / and likewise Udakasevikā, Hara then granted them a boon:

4.136.s:
bhuktvārhopagatāṃ caitāṃ jarattarutale sthitām ..
sevayiṣyaṃti ye bhaktyā jalasaṃpūrṇakaṃḍukaiḥ .. 4.136.20 ..
4.136.d:
भुक्त्वार्होपगतां चैतां जरत्तरुतले स्थिताम् ॥
सेवयिष्यंति ये भक्त्या जलसंपूर्णकंडुकैः ॥ 4.136.20 ॥
4.136.m: 'Those who, with devotion, will attend upon her with pots filled with water, / when she has eaten and come to a worthy [state], staying beneath an aged tree, […]'

4.136.s:
candanena samālabhya puṣpadhūpairathārcya tām ..
bhojayetkṣiprayā caiva kṛśarāpūpapāyasaiḥ .. 21 ..
4.136.d:
चन्दनेन समालभ्य पुष्पधूपैरथार्च्य ताम् ॥
भोजयेत्क्षिप्रया चैव कृशरापूपपायसैः ॥ 21 ॥
4.136.m: Anointing her with sandalwood and then worshipping her with flowers and incense, / he should feed her with kṛśara, rice-cakes, and milk-rice quickly.

4.136.s:
ya evaṃ kurute devi bhaktibhāvena bhāvitaḥ ..
sa putrapaśuvṛddhiṃ ca śarīrārogyamāpnuyāt .. 22 ..
4.136.d:
य एवं कुरुते देवि भक्तिभावेन भावितः ॥
स पुत्रपशुवृद्धिं च शरीरारोग्यमाप्नुयात् ॥ 22 ॥
4.136.m: O goddess, whoever does this, filled with devotion, / obtains increase of sons and cattle, and bodily health.

4.136.s:
na śākinyo gṛhe tasya na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ ..
pīḍāṃ kurvaṃti śiśavo yāṃti vṛddhiṃ nirāmayāḥ .. 23 ..
4.136.d:
न शाकिन्यो गृहे तस्य न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः ॥
पीडां कुर्वंति शिशवो यांति वृद्धिं निरामयाः ॥ 23 ॥
4.136.m: Neither śākinīs, nor piśācas, nor rākṣasas / cause affliction in his house; his children grow free from illness.

4.136.s:
.. yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
kadā pūjā prakartavyā bhūtamātuḥ sukhārthibhiḥ ..
puruṣaiḥ puruṣavyāghra yattanme vaktumarhasi .. 24 ..
4.136.d:
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
कदा पूजा प्रकर्तव्या भूतमातुः सुखार्थिभिः ॥
पुरुषैः पुरुषव्याघ्र यत्तन्मे वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 24 ॥
4.136.m:
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
When should worship of the mother of spirits be performed by men desiring happiness, / O tiger among men? You should tell me this.

4.136.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
sarvatraiṣā bhagavatī bālānāṃ hitakāriṇī ..
nāmabhedaiḥ kriyābhedaiḥ kālabhedaiśca pūjyate .. 25 ..
4.136.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
सर्वत्रैषा भगवती बालानां हितकारिणी ॥
नामभेदैः क्रियाभेदैः कालभेदैश्च पूज्यते ॥ 25 ॥
4.136.m:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Everywhere this goddess benefits children; / she is worshipped under various names, with various rites, and at various times.

4.136.s:
pratipatprabhṛti jyeṣṭhe yāvatpaṃcadaśī tithiḥ ..
tāvatpūjā prakartavyā preraṇaiḥ prekṣaṇīyakaiḥ .. 26 ..
4.136.d:
प्रतिपत्प्रभृति ज्येष्ठे यावत्पंचदशी तिथिः ॥
तावत्पूजा प्रकर्तव्या प्रेरणैः प्रेक्षणीयकैः ॥ 26 ॥
4.136.m: From the first lunar day up to the fifteenth lunar day in Jyeṣṭha, / the worship should be performed through stimulating theatrical shows.

4.136.s:
vikarmaphalanirdeśaḥ pāṃḍavānāṃ viḍaṃbanam..
pradṛśyaṃte hāsyaparairnarairadbhutaceṣṭitaiḥ .. 27 ..
4.136.d:
विकर्मफलनिर्देशः पांडवानां विडंबनम्॥
प्रदृश्यंते हास्यपरैर्नरैरद्भुतचेष्टितैः ॥ 27 ॥
4.136.m: The pointing out of the fruits of bad deeds, the mocking of the Pāṇḍavas, / are exhibited by men intent on humor, through wondrous acts:

4.136.s:
viśvāsyadhanalobhena saṃdhyāyāṃ nihataḥ pathi ..
ārohaṇaṃ ca śūlāgre na paśyaṃtaṃ hi paśyati .. 28 ..
4.136.d:
विश्वास्यधनलोभेन संध्यायां निहतः पथि ॥
आरोहणं च शूलाग्रे न पश्यंतं हि पश्यति ॥ 28 ॥
4.136.m: "Through greed for wealth entrusted [to him], he was killed at twilight on the road; / indeed, he who looks does not see the mounting upon the stake's point!"

4.136.s:
dṛṣṭo bhavadbhiḥ saṃhṛṣṭaḥ parapārāvamarśakaḥ ..
chittvā svahastairyaddatto vibhunā mukhyamodakaḥ .. 29 ..
4.136.d:
दृष्टो भवद्भिः संहृष्टः परपारावमर्शकः ॥
छित्त्वा स्वहस्तैर्यद्दत्तो विभुना मुख्यमोदकः ॥ 29 ॥
4.136.m: "Did you see the delighted toucher of another's wife, / when the principal sweetmeat was given by the lord after cutting off [her lover's organs] with his own hands?"

4.136.s:
śīrṇasūkṣmeṇa patreṇa bālā mālānumoditāḥ ..
muṣkabhugrāsamārūḍho mukhaṃ kṛtvā ca paścime .. 4.136.30 ..
4.136.d:
शीर्णसूक्ष्मेण पत्रेण बाला मालानुमोदिताः ॥
मुष्कभुग्रासमारूढो मुखं कृत्वा च पश्चिमे ॥ 4.136.30 ॥
4.136.m: "With a withered, fine leaf, children rejoice in a garland! / Having climbed atop a scrotum-eating mouthful, and having faced the west—"

4.136.s:
he janāḥ kiṃ na paśyadhvaṃ svāmidrohakaraṃ param ..
karapatrairvidāryaṃtamucchalacchoṇitacchaṭam..31..
4.136.d:
हे जनाः किं न पश्यध्वं स्वामिद्रोहकरं परम् ॥
करपत्रैर्विदार्यंतमुच्छलच्छोणितच्छटम्॥31॥
4.136.m: "O people! Do you not see the greatest betrayer of his master / being torn with saws, with spurting streams of blood?"

4.136.s:
caraiḥ kilāsaiḥ saṃprāptaḥ sarvodvegakaraḥ param ..
daṃḍaprahārābhihato nīyate daṃḍapāśikaiḥ .. 32 ..
4.136.d:
चरैः किलासैः संप्राप्तः सर्वोद्वेगकरः परम् ॥
दंडप्रहाराभिहतो नीयते दंडपाशिकैः ॥ 32 ॥
4.136.m: "He who caused great agitation to all has been caught by the spies with leprous spots! / Struck with blows of sticks, he is led away by the noose-and-staff bearers!"

4.136.s:
prekṣakairveṣṭitaḥ steno raṭatyeṣa vimohitaḥ ..
saṃyamya nīyateyaṃ tu mūrkhaḥ krauryāvilekṣaṇaḥ .. 33 ..
4.136.d:
प्रेक्षकैर्वेष्टितः स्तेनो रटत्येष विमोहितः ॥
संयम्य नीयतेयं तु मूर्खः क्रौर्याविलेक्षणः ॥ 33 ॥
4.136.m: "Surrounded by spectators, this thief babbles, completely bewildered! / Bound, this fool with eyes clouded by cruelty is led away!"

4.136.s:
sitakeśaṃ sitaśmaśrusitāṃbaradharaṃ dvijam ..
vaṭaceṣṭācapeṭābhirhanyamānaṃ na paśyata .. 34 ..
4.136.d:
सितकेशं सितश्मश्रुसितांबरधरं द्विजम् ॥
वटचेष्टाचपेटाभिर्हन्यमानं न पश्यत ॥ 34 ॥
4.136.m: "Do you not see the twice-born with white hair, white beard, and white garments / being beaten with slaps that mimic boys' antics?"

4.136.s:
gṛhānniṣkramyatāṃ raṃḍā vṛddho bhūtvāpyasau striyāḥ ..
svasyā asau na kurute mūḍho bharaṇapoṣaṇam .. 35 ..
4.136.d:
गृहान्निष्क्रम्यतां रंडा वृद्धो भूत्वाप्यसौ स्त्रियाः ॥
स्वस्या असौ न कुरुते मूढो भरणपोषणम् ॥ 35 ॥
4.136.m: "Let the widow be cast out of the house! Though he has grown old, / this foolish man does not provide maintenance and food for his own wife!"

4.136.s:
bhairavābharaṇottālā vyālayajñopavītinaḥ ..
pradattvātāṇḍavapadānpaśyadhvaṃ dhvāṃtadīpakān .. 36 ..
4.136.d:
भैरवाभरणोत्ताला व्यालयज्ञोपवीतिनः ॥
प्रदत्त्वाताण्डवपदान्पश्यध्वं ध्वांतदीपकान् ॥ 36 ॥
4.136.m: "Eminent with terrifying ornaments, wearing snakes as sacred threads, / see them illuminating the darkness, executing steps of the tāṇḍava dance!"

4.136.s:
nirvedako'sya hṛdaye na kiṃcidapi tiṣṭhati ..
gṛhītaṃ yadanenedaṃ bālenāpi mahāvratam .. 37 ..
4.136.d:
निर्वेदकोऽस्य हृदये न किंचिदपि तिष्ठति ॥
गृहीतं यदनेनेदं बालेनापि महाव्रतम् ॥ 37 ॥
4.136.m: "Not the least disgust remains in his heart, / since this great vow was undertaken by him even as a child!"

4.136.s:
raktadṛkkākakṛṣṇāṃgaṃ śabaraṃ kiṃ na paśyata ..
tarukoṭarāṃtaragatāṃśchitvā ca śukaśāvakān .. 38 ..
4.136.d:
रक्तदृक्काककृष्णांगं शबरं किं न पश्यत ॥
तरुकोटरांतरगतांश्छित्वा च शुकशावकान् ॥ 38 ॥
4.136.m: "Do you not see the Śabara with red eyes and a body black as a crow, / having slaughtered the fledglings of parrots dwelling inside the tree-hollow?"

4.136.s:
bahubhiḥ koṣṭhakīkṛtya śaraughaiḥ śakalīkṛtam ..
vimuktaḍhakkāhaṃkārasuprahāraṃ nirīkṣata .. 39 ..
4.136.d:
बहुभिः कोष्ठकीकृत्य शरौघैः शकलीकृतम् ॥
विमुक्तढक्काहंकारसुप्रहारं निरीक्षत ॥ 39 ॥
4.136.m: "Having penned [him] up with many [men], he was cut to pieces with streams of arrows; / behold the excellent blows with unleashed arrogance of ḍhakkā-drums!"

4.136.s:
imāṃ kṛṣṇārddhavadanāṃ gṛhītāṃ siṃdurārcitām ..
vimuktakeśāṃ nṛtyaṃtīṃ paśyadhvaṃ yoginīmiva .. 4.136.40 ..
4.136.d:
इमां कृष्णार्द्धवदनां गृहीतां सिंदुरार्चिताम् ॥
विमुक्तकेशां नृत्यंतीं पश्यध्वं योगिनीमिव ॥ 4.136.40 ॥
4.136.m: "See this woman, half of whose face is black, seized, worshipped with vermilion, / her hair disheveled, dancing like a yoginī,

4.136.s:
gaṃbhīratūryadhvaninā prabuddhāṃ vṛttatāṃḍavām ..
evaṃ prekṣaṇakaṃ kṛtvā nayetvṛkṣatale ca tām ..41..
4.136.d:
गंभीरतूर्यध्वनिना प्रबुद्धां वृत्ततांडवाम् ॥
एवं प्रेक्षणकं कृत्वा नयेत्वृक्षतले च ताम् ॥41॥
4.136.m: awakened by the deep sound of musical instruments, performing the tāṇḍava circle!" / Having thus staged a theatrical show, one should escort her beneath a tree.

4.136.s:
evaṃ kṛte na dāridryaṃ na ca duḥkhaṃ bhavennṛṇām .. 42 ..
rakṣābandhanavarṇanam
4.136.d:
एवं कृते न दारिद्र्यं न च दुःखं भवेन्नृणाम् ॥ 42 ॥
रक्षाबन्धनवर्णनम्
4.136.m:
When this is done, there will be neither poverty nor sorrow for men.
Description of Rakṣābandhana

4.137.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi balirakṣāvidhiṃ nṛpa ..
taṃ śṛṇvekāgramanasā samāsādgaditaṃ mayā .. 1 ..
4.137.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
अथातः संप्रवक्ष्यामि बलिरक्षाविधिं नृप ॥
तं शृण्वेकाग्रमनसा समासाद्गदितं मया ॥ 1 ॥
4.137.m:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
Now, O king, I will proclaim the rule of the protective rite for Bali; / listen to it with a focused mind, as it is told in brief by me.

4.137.s:
purā devāsure yuddhe dānavā suranirjitāḥ ..
śukraṃ baliṃ puraḥ kṛtvā yayuḥ śukra uvāca tam ..2..
4.137.d:
पुरा देवासुरे युद्धे दानवा सुरनिर्जिताः ॥
शुक्रं बलिं पुरः कृत्वा ययुः शुक्र उवाच तम् ॥2॥
4.137.m: Formerly, in the war between gods and asuras, the dānavas were conquered by the gods. / Placing Śukra and Bali in front, they went [to him]; Śukra said to him:

4.137.s:
.. śakra uvāca .. ..
na viṣādastvayā kāryaḥ kāryāṇāṃ gatirīdṛśī..
daivādbhavaṃti bhūtānāṃ kāle jayaparājayāḥ.. 3 ..
4.137.d:
॥ शक्र उवाच ॥ ॥
न विषादस्त्वया कार्यः कार्याणां गतिरीदृशी॥
दैवाद्भवंति भूतानां काले जयपराजयाः॥ 3 ॥
4.137.m:
Śukra said:
You should not grieve; such is the course of affairs. / Victory and defeat happen to beings by fate in the course of time.

4.137.s:
saṃdhānaṃ saha śakreṇa kriyatāmayanadvayama ..
ajeyaḥ sarvaśatrūṇāṃ kṛtaḥ śacyā śacīpatiḥ.. 4 ..
4.137.d:
संधानं सह शक्रेण क्रियतामयनद्वयम ॥
अजेयः सर्वशत्रूणां कृतः शच्या शचीपतिः॥ 4 ॥
4.137.m: Make peace with Śakra for two half-years. / Śacī's lord was made invincible to all enemies by Śacī.

4.137.s:
rakṣābaṃdhaprabhāvena dānavendro jito mahān ..
varṣamekaṃ pratīkṣasva tataḥ śreyo bhaviṣyati .. 5 ..
4.137.d:
रक्षाबंधप्रभावेन दानवेन्द्रो जितो महान् ॥
वर्षमेकं प्रतीक्षस्व ततः श्रेयो भविष्यति ॥ 5 ॥
4.137.m: By the power of tying the protective amulet, the great lord of dānavas was conquered. / Wait for one year; after that, your welfare will come to pass.

4.137.s:
bhārgaveṇaivamuktāste dānavā vigatajvarāḥ ..
tasthuḥ kālaṃ pratīkṣanto yathoktaṃ guruṇā tathā ..6..
4.137.d:
भार्गवेणैवमुक्तास्ते दानवा विगतज्वराः ॥
तस्थुः कालं प्रतीक्षन्तो यथोक्तं गुरुणा तथा ॥6॥
4.137.m: Thus spoken to by the descendant of Bhṛgu, those dānavas became free from distress; / they remained awaiting the time, exactly as spoken by their guru.

4.137.s:
eṣa prabhāvo rakṣāyāḥ kathitaste yudhiṣṭhira ..
jayadaḥ sukhadaścaiva putrārogyadhanapradaḥ ..7..
4.137.d:
एष प्रभावो रक्षायाः कथितस्ते युधिष्ठिर ॥
जयदः सुखदश्चैव पुत्रारोग्यधनप्रदः ॥7॥
4.137.m: This power of the protective amulet has been told to you, O Yudhiṣṭhira; / it grants victory and happiness, and bestows sons, health, and wealth.

4.137.s:
.. yudhiṣṭhira uvāca .. ..
kriyate kena vidhinā rakṣābaṃdhaḥ surottama ..
kasyāṃ tithau kadā deva etanme vaktumarhasi .. 8 ..
4.137.d:
॥ युधिष्ठिर उवाच ॥ ॥
क्रियते केन विधिना रक्षाबंधः सुरोत्तम ॥
कस्यां तिथौ कदा देव एतन्मे वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 8 ॥
4.137.m:
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
By what procedure is the tying of the protective amulet performed, O best of gods? / On what lunar day and when, O Lord? You should tell me this.

4.137.s:
yathā yathā hi bhagavānvicitrāṇi prabhāṣate ..
tathā tathā na me tṛptirbahvarthāḥ śṛṇvataḥ kathāḥ .. 9 ..
4.137.d:
यथा यथा हि भगवान्विचित्राणि प्रभाषते ॥
तथा तथा न मे तृप्तिर्बह्वर्थाः शृण्वतः कथाः ॥ 9 ॥
4.137.m: For as the Lord speaks of wondrous things, / so my satisfaction is never filled, hearing these accounts rich in meaning.

4.137.s:
.. śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca .. ..
ghanāvṛte'mbare pārtha śādvale dharaṇītale ..
saṃprāpte śrāvaṇe caiva paurṇamāsyāṃ dinodaye .. 4.137.10 ..
4.137.d:
॥ श्रीकृष्ण उवाच ॥ ॥
घनावृतेऽम्बरे पार्थ शाद्वले धरणीतले ॥
संप्राप्ते श्रावणे चैव पौर्णमास्यां दिनोदये ॥ 4.137.10 ॥
4.137.m:
Śrī Kṛṣṇa said:
When the sky is covered with clouds, O son of Pṛthā, when the surface of the earth is grassy, / and Śrāvaṇa has arrived, at daybreak on the full moon,

4.137.s:
snānaṃ kurvīta matimāñśrutismṛtividhānata ..
tato devānpitṝṃścaiva tarpayetparamāṃbhasā .. 11 ..
4.137.d:
स्नानं कुर्वीत मतिमाञ्श्रुतिस्मृतिविधानत ॥
ततो देवान्पितॄंश्चैव तर्पयेत्परमांभसा ॥ 11 ॥
4.137.m: the wise man should bathe according to the rules of Śruti and Smṛti; / then he should make water-offerings to the gods and ancestors with excellent water.

4.137.s:
upākarmādivedoktamṛṣīṇāṃ caiva tarpaṇam ..
kuryuśca brāhmaṇāḥ śrāddhaṃ devamuddiśya śaktitaḥ .. 12 ..
4.137.d:
उपाकर्मादिवेदोक्तमृषीणां चैव तर्पणम् ॥
कुर्युश्च ब्राह्मणाः श्राद्धं देवमुद्दिश्य शक्तितः ॥ 12 ॥
4.137.m: The brāhmaṇas should perform the upākarma and other rites prescribed in the Vedas, the offering of water to the ṛṣis, / and a śrāddha dedicated to the god according to their ability.

4.137.s: śūdrāṇāṃ maṃtrasahitaṃ snānaṃ dānaṃ ca śasyate .. 13 ..
4.137.d: शूद्राणां मंत्रसहितं स्नानं दानं च शस्यते ॥ 13 ॥
4.137.m: For śūdras, bathing and giving gifts accompanied by mantras are recommended.

4.137.s:
tatoparāhnasamaye rakṣāpoṭalikāḥ śubhāḥ ..
kārayeccākṣataiḥ śastaiḥ siddhārthairhemabhūṣitāḥ .. 14 ..
4.137.d:
ततोपराह्नसमये रक्षापोटलिकाः शुभाः ॥
कारयेच्चाक्षतैः शस्तैः सिद्धार्थैर्हेमभूषिताः ॥ 14 ॥
4.137.m: Then, in the afternoon, auspicious protective packets / should be made with unblemished whole grains and white mustard seeds, adorned with gold,

4.137.s:
vastrairvicitraiḥ kārpāsaiḥ kṣaumairvā malavarjitaiḥ ..
vicitratarairgrathitāḥ sthāpayedbhā janopari .. 15 ..
4.137.d:
वस्त्रैर्विचित्रैः कार्पासैः क्षौमैर्वा मलवर्जितैः ॥
विचित्रतरैर्ग्रथिताः स्थापयेद्भा जनोपरि ॥ 15 ॥
4.137.m: with diverse, spotless cotton or linen cloths; / woven in very colorful patterns, he should place them upon a vessel.

4.137.s:
kāryā gṛhasya rakṣā gomayarahitaiḥ suvṛttakuṃḍūkaiḥ ..
dūrvāvarṇakasahitaiḥ sakaladuṣkṛtopaśāṃtaye .. 16 ..
4.137.d:
कार्या गृहस्य रक्षा गोमयरहितैः सुवृत्तकुंडूकैः ॥
दूर्वावर्णकसहितैः सकलदुष्कृतोपशांतये ॥ 16 ॥
4.137.m: Protection of the house is to be made with well-rounded balls free of cow dung, / accompanied by dūrvā grass and pigments, for the pacification of all misdeeds.

4.137.s:
upaliptagṛhamadhye catuṣkopari nyasecchubhaṃ pīṭham ..
tatropaviśedrājā sāmātyaḥ sapurohitaḥ sasuhṛt .. 17 ..
4.137.d:
उपलिप्तगृहमध्ये चतुष्कोपरि न्यसेच्छुभं पीठम् ॥
तत्रोपविशेद्राजा सामात्यः सपुरोहितः ससुहृत् ॥ 17 ॥
4.137.m: In the middle of the plastered house, upon a square diagram, one should set down an auspicious seat; / there the king should sit with his ministers, chaplain, and friends,

4.137.s:
veśyājanenasahito maṃgalaśabdaiḥ suhasitaiścihnaiḥ..
rakṣābaṃdhaḥ kāryaḥ śāṃtidhvaninā narendrasya..18..
4.137.d:
वेश्याजनेनसहितो मंगलशब्दैः सुहसितैश्चिह्नैः॥
रक्षाबंधः कार्यः शांतिध्वनिना नरेन्द्रस्य॥18॥
4.137.m: together with courtesans, with auspicious sounds and smiling signs; / the tying of the protective amulet for the ruler of men should be performed with sounds of peace.

4.137.s:
devadvijātiśastā sustrīrarghyaiḥ samarcayetprathamam..
tadanu purodhā nṛpatiṃ rakṣāṃ badhnīta maṃtreṇa..19..
4.137.d:
देवद्विजातिशस्ता सुस्त्रीरर्घ्यैः समर्चयेत्प्रथमम्॥
तदनु पुरोधा नृपतिं रक्षां बध्नीत मंत्रेण॥19॥
4.137.m: First he should worship with offerings of honor virtuous women praised by gods and twice-born; / afterwards, the royal priest should tie the protective amulet on the king with the mantra:

4.137.s:
yena baddho balī rājā dānavendro mahābalaḥ .
tena tvāmabhibadhnāmi rakṣe mā cala mā cala . . 4.137.20
4.137.d:
येन बद्धो बली राजा दानवेन्द्रो महाबलः ।
तेन त्वामभिबध्नामि रक्षे मा चल मा चल ॥ 4.137.20
4.137.m: "By which the powerful King Bali, the very mighty lord of dānavas, was bound, / with that I bind you; O protective amulet, do not slip away, do not slip away!"

4.137.s:
brāhmaṇaiḥ kṣatriyairvaiśyaiḥ śūdraiścānyaiśca mānavaiḥ .
kartavyo rakṣikābandho dvijānsampūjya bhaktitaḥ . . 21
4.137.d:
ब्राह्मणैः क्षत्रियैर्वैश्यैः शूद्रैश्चान्यैश्च मानवैः ।
कर्तव्यो रक्षिकाबन्धो द्विजान्सम्पूज्य भक्तितः ॥ 21
4.137.m:
By Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, Śūdras, and other men,
the tying of the amulet is to be performed after revering the twice-born with devotion.

4.137.s:
anena vidhinā yastu rakṣikābandhamācaret .
sa sarvadoṣarahitaḥ sukhī samvatsaraṃ bhavet . . 22
4.137.d:
अनेन विधिना यस्तु रक्षिकाबन्धमाचरेत् ।
स सर्वदोषरहितः सुखी सम्वत्सरं भवेत् ॥ 22
4.137.m:
Whoever performs the tying of the amulet according to this rule
becomes free from all faults and happy for a year.

4.137.s:
yaḥ śrāvaṇe sravati śītajale narendra rakṣāvidhānavidhimācarate manuṣyaḥ .
āste sukhena parameṇa ca sarvamekaḥ putraprapautrasahitaḥ sasuhṛdvṛtaśca . . 23
4.137.d:
यः श्रावणे स्रवति शीतजले नरेन्द्र रक्षाविधानविधिमाचरते मनुष्यः ।
आस्ते सुखेन परमेण च सर्वमेकः पुत्रप्रपौत्रसहितः ससुहृद्वृतश्च ॥ 23
4.137.m:
The man who performs the rite of the protection-ordinance in Śrāvaṇa when cold water flows, O king,
abides alone in supreme happiness with sons and great-grandsons, surrounded by his friends, for the whole [year].

4.137.s:
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇa uttaraparvaṇi śrīkṛṣṇayudhiṣṭhirasaṃvāde
śrāvaṇapūrṇimārakṣābandhanavidhivarṇanaṃ nāma saptatriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ . 137
mahānavamīvratavarṇanam
4.137.d:
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराण उत्तरपर्वणि श्रीकृष्णयुधिष्ठिरसंवादे
श्रावणपूर्णिमारक्षाबन्धनविधिवर्णनं नाम सप्तत्रिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः । 137
महानवमीव्रतवर्णनम्
4.137.m:
Thus ends the one hundred and thirty-seventh chapter, named 'Description of the Rite of Tying the Protection [Amulet] on the Full Moon of Śrāvaṇa', in the dialogue between Śrī Kṛṣṇa and Yudhiṣṭhira, in the Uttaraparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of the Mahānavamī Votive Observance
